chapter.subject: Science
chapter.chapter: Chapter 7 — Work, Energy, and Simple Machines

excerpts:
[INJSO 2009 — question paper]
1. Which one of the following expressions has the same units as power?
a) Force x distance
b) Work x time
¢) Force x acceleration
d) Force x velocity

[INJSO 2010 — question paper]
46. A trolley runs from point P to Q along a track, as shown in the figure. At point Q,
its potential energy is 50 kJ less than at point P. At point P, the trolley has kinetic energy
5 kJ. Between P and Q, the work done against friction is 10 kJ. What is the kinetic energy
at point Q?
a) 35 kJ b) 45 kJ c) 55 kJ d) 65 kJ

[INJSO 2012 — question paper]
1. A load is to be moved using a wheelbarrow. The total mass of the load and wheelbarrow is 60 kg.
The magnitude of gravitational acceleration is 10 ms 2 .
What is the work done if the handle is raised by 50 cm?
a) 35.0 J
b) 17.5 J
c) 175 J
d) 350 J

[INJSO 2012 — question paper]
45. The diagram shows a lift system in which the elevator (mass m 1 ) is partly counterbalanced by a
heavy weight (mass m 2 ).
At what rate does the motor provide energy to the system when the elevator is rising at a steady
speed v ? (g = acceleration of free fall) (consider the pulley as frictionless at the pivot)
a) (m 1 + m 2 )gv
b) ½ (m 1 + m 2 )gv
c) (m 1 m 2 )gv /(m 1 + m 2 )
d) (m 1 – m 2 )gv

items.stem: Which of the following is the scientific definition of work done by a constant force?
A trolley moves from point P to Q. Its potential energy decreases by 50 kJ, and the work done against friction is 10 kJ. If its initial kinetic energy at P is 5 kJ, what is its kinetic energy at Q?
A lift system has an elevator of mass m₁ and a counterweight of mass m₂. The elevator rises at a steady speed. What is the rate at which the motor provides energy to the system?
If a force of 10 N displaces an object by 2 m in the direction of the force, what is the work done?
A person applies a force of 100 N to push a box 5 m in the same direction as the force. What is the work done by the person on the box?
A worker applies a force of 200 N to lift a 50 kg box vertically. The box is lifted 2 m. What is the work done by the worker on the box?
In a carrom game, a striker moves 0.2 m and applies a force on a white coin. The white coin then moves 0.1 m and applies a force on a black coin. Which of the following statements is true?
A block is pulled by a force of 150 N, and it moves 4 m. The force is applied at an angle of 60° to the displacement. What is the work done by the force on the block?
Which form of energy is directly connected to the forces and motions studied earlier?
A force of 100 N is applied to a box, and it moves 3 m in the direction of the force. What is the work done by the force on the box?
What is the SI unit of kinetic energy?
A car of mass 1000 kg is moving with a velocity of 20 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
According to the passage, what happens to an object's kinetic energy when negative work is done on it?
What is the term used to describe the energy stored in an object due to its deformation or in a system of objects due to their relative positions?
In which of the following scenarios is the potential energy of an object increased?
According to the passage, what happens to the potential energy of a ball when it is lifted to a greater height above the Earth's surface?
A ball of mass 0.5 kg is thrown vertically upward with a velocity of 10 m/s. What is the maximum height it will reach? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
A ball of mass m is lifted to a height of 2 meters from the ground and then released. What is the work done by the gravitational force as the ball falls to the ground?
A ball is dropped from a height h and collides with the ground. After the collision, it bounces back to a height less than h. Which of the following best explains this phenomenon?

A 60 kg man rides a scooter of mass 100 kg. The next day, his 40 kg son joins him. If the scooter reaches the same speed on both days in the same time, what is the ratio of the fuel used on the two days?
A student is lifted straight up in an elevator and then climbs the stairs to the same height. What can be said about the change in their potential energy in both cases?
A coconut of mass 1.5 kg falls from a 10 m high tree. What is the velocity of the coconut just before it hits the sand?

The potential energy-displacement graph of a 0.5 kg ball moving along a frictionless track is shown. At position O, the ball has 30 J of potential energy and 0 m/s. What is the velocity of the ball at position P?

A seesaw is balanced when the product of the mass and distance from the fulcrum on both sides is equal. If a 15 kg child sits 2 m from the fulcrum, where should a 30 kg child sit to balance the seesaw?
A lever is used to lift a heavy object. If the effort arm is 4 m and the load arm is 2 m, what is the mechanical advantage of the lever?

A lift system uses a counterweight to reduce the work done by the motor. If the elevator has a mass of 1000 kg and the counterweight has a mass of 800 kg, what is the rate at which the motor must provide energy to raise the elevator at a steady speed of 2 m/s?

A watermill converts potential energy into kinetic energy as water flows from a higher point to a lower point. If the potential energy of water at the top is 5000 J and 1000 J is lost due to friction, what is the kinetic energy at the bottom?

A trolley moves from point P to Q, losing 50 kJ of potential energy and doing 10 kJ of work against friction. If the trolley has 5 kJ of kinetic energy at point P, what is its kinetic energy at point Q?
According to the passage, what happens to the force required to lift a load as the length of the inclined plane increases?
A person uses an inclined plane to lift a 50 kg load to a height of 2 m. If the length of the inclined plane is 10 m, what is the force required to lift the load (assuming no friction)?
What is the SI unit of power?
A ball is dropped from different heights into sand. The depth of the depression created in the sand is directly related to which of the following?
A 100 N load is being lifted using an inclined plane. If the mechanical advantage is 5, what is the force applied by the person?
What is the unit of potential energy?
What is the SI unit of power?
What is the primary purpose of using an inclined plane to lift a heavy object?
A car of mass 1000 kg starts from rest and reaches a speed of 72 km/h in 10 seconds. What is the power of the engine required to achieve this?
What is the SI unit of work and energy?
When the displacement of an object is perpendicular to the direction of the force, what is the work done on the object?
A person lifts a 5 kg bag to a height of 3 m. How much work is done by the person?
A ball of mass 2 kg is thrown vertically upwards. What is the sign of the work done by gravity on the ball during its upward motion?
In which of the following cases is no work done on the object?
